newsitem.title: USA: Ethanol issue left out of US budget pact.
newsitem.headline: Ethanol issue left out of US budget pact.

text.p: Congressional Republicans failed to settle ethanol issues when they crafted their unified tax proposal, but left them to be addressed in budget meetings with the White House, a key senator said Wednesday.

"Today, the Senate Republican conferees followed the request of Senator Grassley in leaving the question of accepting the ethanol tax incentive to the next phase of the conference negotiations," a statement from the Iowa Republican's office said.

Senate tax legislation would extend the subsidy for producers of the corn-based fuel until 2007, paring it down modestly in that period. The House bill would leave the subsidy intact but end it as scheduled in 2000.
